content.title: Madonna’s ‘Popular’ Is Becoming A Career-Defining Hit For The Singer
content.text: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 12: Madonna speaks onstage during the 2021 MTV Video Music Awards at Barclays Center on September 12, 2021 in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. (Photo by Theo Wargo/Getty Images for MTV/ViacomCBS)Getty Images for MTV/ViacomCBSMadonna has been charting hit singles around the world for decades. She first reached the ranking of the most popular songs in the U.K. back in 1984, and since then, she’s been doling out smash after smash. This week, the pop superstar’s latest cut is still going strong, and now it’s reached a special milestone in the nation.“Popular” hits 30 weeks spent on the U.K. singles chart as of this frame. The tune, which features Madonna and Playboy Carti and which is fronted by The Weeknd, is not just present, it’s doing very well. It’s only the second hit from the singer to make it to that 30-week milestone.This week, “Popular” falls slightly, dipping from No. 13 to No. 16. The tune is pushed down, in part, by a handful of exciting new releases that earn lofty debuts. Beyoncé’s “Texas Hold ‘Em” opens at No. 9, while Kanye West and Ty Dolla $ign’s “Carnival” launches at No. 12. Madonna does beat West and $ign’s other two new wins, “Burn” and “Back to Me,” which start at Nos. 17 and 18, respectively.“Popular” now ranks as the second-longest-charting hit of Madonna’s career in the U.K. Last week, it was tied with “4 Minutes,” which features both Justin Timberlake and Timbaland. That tune, which fronted her album Hard Candy, racked up 29 turns on the tally starting in the spring of 2008.The Madonna single that has spent the most time on the U.K. songs chart remains “Hung Up.” That dance smash lived on the ranking for 40 weeks nearly two decades ago. “Popular” is still very, well, popular, in the country, but whether it can hold on for another 10 frames and match–and perhaps even top–”Hung Up” is hard to predict. It is still living inside the top 20, so it seems like it will stick around for a while, but exactly how long is anyone’s guess.MORE FROM FORBES ADVISORJust a few weeks ago, “Popular” helped Madonna make history in the U.K. After months of climbing the chart and living just below the loftiest tier, the single finally broke into the top 10. It peaked at No. 10, giving the superstar her sixty-fourth placement inside the highest region on the ranking.ForbesMadonna Makes Chart History With Her First Top 10 Hit In 15 YearsBy Hugh McIntyre Email Address
